At least the kid was on time! The problem for the student occurs when the student is cutting it too close every single time, and then a hiccup/traffic jam occurs driving to school, walking across campus, and/or weaving through crowded hallways, and the student gets to class after the teacher starts teaching. Then there is a problem, and then I would not appreciate the tardiness. Because you are currently a college student, my advice is that you aim to arrive at least 15 minutes before class starts. When you start working a full-time job, a good mantra is “If you’re on time, you’re late,” meaning if you are entering the building at exactly the minute you are supposed to start working, it’s not good. Try to be in the building and at (or really near) your desk maybe 15 minutes before your shift starts.
